channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: Alaska elects Mary Peltola over Sen. Dan Sullivan (R), AP reports, giving Democrats a 56-44 edge in the Senate
item.description: The race was the last to be called in the Senate, securing Democrats a historic sweep of nine new seats. Peltola, a former congresswoman, is one of two Indigenous women ever elected to the Senate.

item.title: What we know about why everything seems to be breaking at once
item.description: Microsoft’s Outlook emails, air traffic control, JPMorgan Chase and United Airlines were among the high-profile systems that had outages in the past week. Experts say the interruptions don’t seem to be connected, but everyone wants answers.

item.title: White House pulls nomination of Heidi Overton to lead Food and Drug Administration following bipartisan pushback
item.description: The decision came amid growing concerns that she could not be confirmed by the Senate to lead the agency charged with overseeing the safety of drugs, vaccines, tobacco and the majority of the U.S. food supply, according to a White House official and three other people familiar with the matter. Overton had been slated to get a vote Wednesday before a Senate committee.

item.title: How much life could a 10-minute walk buy you? Try our calculator.
item.description: Researchers calculated how spending more time moving each day may pay off in the future. See what you could gain from adding more daily movement to your life.

item.title: FAA oversaw and signed off on repair work before nationwide ground stop
item.description: A person familiar with the investigation said blame placed on contractor L3Harris overlooked the role of the Federal Aviation Administration. An FAA official was supervising a contractor in rural Arkansas as he switched vital air traffic communications lines from a old copper-wire network to a new fiber one, even testing the finished product and signing off on the work, the person said.

item.title: ICE is detaining green-card holders over decades-old, minor violations
item.description: Authorities are detaining people over charges that did not come up when applying for or renewing green cards and that in the past would have resulted in a citation — not an effort to remove legal status.

item.title: ‘The most ominous signal’: Four ways Trump may pivot after the midterm rout
item.description: Two years of a Democratic Congress might push the president to change his views.

item.title: Brazilian federal police are investigating whether JD Vance’s donor network aided Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The probe has drawn renewed attention to the uncommon political partnership between MAGA and the Bolsonaro-led Brazilian right.

item.title: National Security Agency suffers outage of internal communications system used to exchange classified messages
item.description: The reasons for the outage involving NSA Net were not immediately clear. But a former Pentagon official said it was significant enough to force the intelligence agency to delay employees’ arrival times at its headquarters at Fort Meade, Maryland, and other locations.

item.title: Behind deadly Logan Circle shooting, a familiar frustration about housing
item.description: The Logan Circle shooter had complained online and filed a lawsuit about the conditions in his D.C. condo. While his violent response is rare, his anger touched a familiar chord for Washingtonians — from renters to condo owners — who complain about festering problems that include inadequate heat, the emergence of mold and the proliferation of vermin.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Husband dillydallies too long to make flight to friend’s wedding
item.description: Husband resisted the letter writer’s travel suggestions at every point yet insists the missed event “wasn’t on purpose.”

item.title: Jensen Huang said he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO in first remarks after resigning amid news of affair with alleged spy
item.description: The company’s founder said in a statement that he has received an outpouring of encouragement to return. Its board said Monday that it was not considering the move.

item.title: U.S. formally loses its status as a country that has eliminated measles
item.description: The designation reverses a landmark public health achievement and acknowledges a new reality: A disease Americans largely stopped having to think about for more than a quarter-century is once again spreading continuously throughout its communities.

item.title: The FAA failed. Naturally, it wants another $50 billion.
item.description: Much of the world has figured out a better way to fund air traffic control.

item.title: Trump pushes more White House renovations in wake of GOP midterm loss
item.description: The president has claimed he is paying for the White House makeover, but the Park Service is set to foot much of the bill.

item.title: Trump in Asia. Nvidia. White House renovations. Green cards. Acquitted mom. Longevity calculator. James Bond. Catch up now.
item.description: Catch up in minutes.

item.title: Lawyers for Saudi national accused of bugging OpenAI say there’s no evidence he’s a spy
item.description: Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked as an engineer at OpenAI, was arrested last month and charged with one count of violating the Wiretap Act for allegedly placing a recording device behind a TV in an executive conference room at the AI company. Prosecutors have not provided any evidence that Alfozan has ties to the Saudi government or was working at its behest, despite providing a set of documents and engaging in two meetings with defense lawyers, Alfozan’s lawyers said in a filing Monday.

item.title: We have a new James Bond. But are we happy about it?
item.description: What’s in store for the next James Bond movie now that director Denis Villeneuve has ended years of rampant speculation and cast the idiosyncratic Robert Pattinson as 007? We have thoughts.

item.title: Mr. President, you’ve picked the wrong golf course
item.description: Mr. President, you’ve picked the wrong golf course

item.title: White House weighs next steps for FDA nominee who faces bipartisan pushback
item.description: Some Republicans, many Democrats and prominent Make America Health Again supporters have questioned or opposed Heidi Overton’s candidacy. Overton serves as the deputy director of the White House’s Domestic Policy Council.

item.title: Student no longer enrolled at law school after The Post reported how he was expelled from college over 2021 sex assault
item.description: The Post found that Tate Weston had gained admission to Washington and Lee University in Virginia after Tulane University determined he was responsible for assaulting a fellow student years ago.

item.title: Colonial Williamsburg unveils $600 million upgrade for its 100th birthday
item.description: The five-year plan will expand the Virginia outdoor history museum’s scope, including a bigger focus on the Constitution and the Bill of Rights, and add new facilities.

item.title: Trump administration proposes restrictions for employer-sponsored green cards
item.description: The Labor Department proposal would require employers looking to sponsor green cards to expand efforts to recruit American workers for those positions, according to a notice published in the Federal Register.

item.title: Our top 5 recommendations for a juicy, flavorful centerpiece for your Thanksgiving meal
item.description: Our top 5 recommendations for a juicy, flavorful centerpiece for your Thanksgiving meal

item.title: The Hegseth impeachment vote was just a warmup for the real thing
item.description: When Democrats take over Congress, the serious effort to remove the defense secretary will begin.

item.title: Trump’s stake in Nvidia grew to as much as $62 million before scandal broke out
item.description: The president benefited from the firm’s success, disclosures show. The value of his holdings rose dramatically as his administration let Nvidia sell advanced chips in China.

item.title: Trump administration orders closure of AI chip loophole at heart of Nvidia scandal
item.description: The move comes as the downfall of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has highlighted gaps in U.S. export controls and exposed a clash between President Donald Trump’s top economic advisers over the issue.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial in murder case in March
item.description: Her first trial ended in a mistrial after the jury was unable to come to a unanimous conclusion about whether she was legally culpable for the killing of her three children.

item.title: The serious complications of GLP-1s that few may know about
item.description: With millions of patients taking GLP-1 drugs, doctors are discovering rare but worrying problems affecting the body and the mind.

item.title: Flight chaos. Weakened Trump. Midterm results. Tulane. Death penalty. GLP-1 complications. Healthiest breakfast. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: 21 habits of people whose homes are always tidy
item.description: Strategies include having designated places for items, cleaning as you cook, scheduling routine chores and making your bed every morning.

item.title: Don’t assume Nvidia will rebound
item.description: The chipmaker’s dependence on its co-founder has become a corporate liability, Megan McArdle writes.

item.title: This joint implant and surgery give people with arthritis a new option
item.description: Here’s why it’s such a big deal, according to the surgeons performing the thumb implant procedure.

item.title: Pentagon prepares its own prosecution of general accused of leaking
item.description: Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia now faces legal jeopardy on two fronts after allegations by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s team were previously referred to the Justice Department.

item.title: Their son died fighting a wildfire. They may never understand why he was even there.
item.description: This has been the third-deadliest year for wildland firefighters since at least 2016, prompting questions about sending crews directly into remote, burning terrain.

item.title: J.K. Rowling’s agent is betting on the books that publishers won’t touch
item.description: A conversation with Neil Blair about High Line, a new home for disfavored titles.

item.title: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blames Congress and prior administrations for air travel halt and ensuing chaos
item.description: Duffy refused to apologize for failures that led to the nationwide ground stop, pointing to a lack of investment in air traffic modernization. President Donald Trump, in his first public comments on the situation, on Sunday specifically blamed the Biden administration.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Take back ex-wife for the sake of being ‘one big happy family’?
item.description: He’s not in love with her anymore but thinks a good dad would remarry his kids’ mom after her health crisis.

item.title: The link between microplastics and one of the deadliest cancers, and what to do
item.description: New evidence points to how particles from Styrofoam cups and take-out containers can make people more vulnerable to colon cancer.

item.title: A university found him responsible for sexual assault. A law school admitted him anyway.
item.description: An accused student’s path through three universities highlights what experts say are gaps in college disciplinary systems.

item.title: FAA was warned for years about repair risks leading to nationwide ground stop
item.description: Officials said installation of a new router was behind the cancellation of thousands of flights. A government watchdog report in September cautioned that the way old, legacy systems were being replaced could result in disruptions — including ground stops.

item.title: Federal judge blocks Trump administration from closing East Potomac Park, where the president wants to redevelop a golf course
item.description: President Donald Trump wants to turn the park’s three-course complex into a single championship course, but golfers and preservationists are suing to block him.

item.title: As a doctor, here’s the easy, make-ahead breakfast I recommend to my patients
item.description: Overnight oats are one of the best breakfasts for your gut and heart.

item.title: The Democratic governor-elect of Texas tells The Post she wants to try something new: Moderation
item.description: Gina Hinojosa said she agrees with President Donald Trump on the need for border security but vows to fight what she called “chaotic and dangerous” immigration enforcement in major cities.

item.title: Why the Nvidia scandal could be a problem for Trump
item.description: What makes ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy an explosive political problem for the White House is that it brings together the very issues that propelled Democrats to victory in the midterms.

item.title: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger reverses state’s plan to participate in Trump’s school vouchers
item.description: A letter from the IRS said the state needs to complete the process begun by former governor Glenn Youngkin. Spanberger said she won’t finish the enrollment.

item.title: Stephen Miller dresses like a reasonable man. But listen to what he says, Robin Givhan writes.
item.description: The new White House chief of staff understands how ordinary menswear can lend familiarity — and legitimacy — to an uncompromising worldview.

item.title: Work to replace old copper wiring led to ground stop, Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy says
item.description: Flight cancellations continue, but FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said Saturday that “the worst is behind us” and that flights around the country should be back on schedule by the end of the weekend, following Friday’s nationwide ground stop.

item.title: The internet won’t necessarily go dark. It could simply stop working.
item.description: AI is exposing decades of software shortcuts. They need fixing before hackers exploit the weaknesses, a Vanderbilt University professor writes.

item.title: A spy plane tied to covert attacks leads back to The Villages, Florida’s retirement mega-community
item.description: The high-tech surveillance plane repeatedly flew in the vicinity of CIA-linked attacks on boats near the Galápagos Islands this year. A Post investigation reveals the role the Morse family — prominent GOP donors and billionaire owners of The Villages — had in the company that once owned the plane. It also reveals a web of contractors that suggests the plane itself has ties to the CIA.
